source_paper: Wang et al. 2026, Naunyn-Schmiedebergs Arch Pharmacol (never sent to the agent; see replication/wang2026/paper_card.md)
question: Is genetically predicted use of each of the following medication classes causally associated with overall lung cancer risk: salicylic acid and derivatives, opioids, antithrombotic agents, thyroid preparations, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, and drugs used in diabetes? For each class, report the effect as an odds ratio of lung cancer per unit increase in the log-odds of using the medication, and say whether it is statistically significant at P<0.05.
data_description:
exposure_drug_use_instruments.tsv: genetic instruments for self-reported use of each medication class, from a large European-ancestry biobank GWAS (cases = people reporting use of the class). One row per (drug, SNP). The SNPs for each drug have already been selected as genome-wide significant (relaxed to P<5e-6 for a drug with too few SNPs) and LD-clumped to be approximately independent. beta = log-odds of medication use per copy of effect_allele, with its standard_error; chromosome and position_grch37 are GRCh37 coordinates.
outcome_lung_cancer.tsv: European-ancestry lung cancer (all histologies) case-control GWAS summary statistics (log-odds betas per effect_allele), restricted to the instrument SNPs. Not every instrument SNP is present.
